cards.text: Malaysia stopped replacing itself in 2013. 2024 brought the fewest babies in over 40 years, and the official projection has the population shrinking from 2059.
cards.sub: The yearly birth drop is reported as a surprise. The decade-long trend, and the peak just ahead, rarely are.
sources: DOSM (TFR below 2.1 since 2013; population peak 2059); DOSM Vital Statistics 2024 (fewest births in 40+ years)

cards.h: The fertility rate was 1.6 in 2024, below the 2.1 needed to hold a population steady, and it has stayed below that line every year since 2013.
cards.s: About 414,918 babies were born in 2024, the fewest in more than four decades.
cards.d: The fertility rate was 1.6 in 2024, below the 2.1 needed to hold a population steady, and it has stayed below that line every year since 2013. About 414,918 babies were born in 2024, the fewest in more than four decades.
sources: DOSM Vital Statistics Malaysia 2024 / Current Population Estimates 2025 (TFR 1.6; below replacement since 2013; live births ~414,918)

cards.h: The statistics department's own projection has the population peaking at 42.38 million in 2059, then declining to 41.43 million by 2070.
cards.s: Public debate still assumes a forever-growing Malaysia; the official numbers already mark the turn.
cards.d: The statistics department's own projection has the population peaking at 42.38 million in 2059, then declining to 41.43 million by 2070. Public debate still assumes a forever-growing Malaysia; the official numbers already mark the turn.
sources: DOSM Population Projections Malaysia (peak 42.38M in 2059; 41.43M by 2070), reported via Malay Mail, 11 Jul 2025

cards.h: Fewer births now means fewer workers later. The same trend drives a fast-ageing population: those 65 and older passed 7% in 2021 and head for 14% by about 2048.
cards.s: A smaller working base must support a larger retired one, the squeeze behind the pension and healthcare bills.
cards.d: Fewer births now means fewer workers later. The same trend drives a fast-ageing population: those 65 and older passed 7% in 2021 and head for 14% by about 2048. A smaller working base must support a larger retired one, the squeeze behind the pension and healthcare bills.
sources: DOSM (65+ crossed 7% in 2021; 14% 'aged nation' by ~2048, band 2044-2048); links to the support-ratio analysis

cards.text: Malaysia debates how to raise the birth rate. The fact already set for the next 30 years, the year the population turns down, is the one nobody plans for.
It is like a reservoir whose inflow fell below its outflow years ago. The level still looks high, but the date it starts to drop is already fixed.
A country can plan for a smaller, older population or be surprised by one. Malaysia's own statisticians have already named the year; the harder task is saying the forecast out loud.

sources: DOSM Population Projections Malaysia (peak 42.38M in 2059); DOSM Current Population Estimates 2025; DOSM Vital Statistics Malaysia 2024 (TFR 1.6; births ~414,918); Malay Mail (11 Jul 2025, citing DOSM); LPPKN/Malaysia Population Research Hub; World Bank Open Data; docs/research/malaysia-underreported-data-forecasts.md (Sections B.3, C). See engine/briefs/fertility-below-replacement-2059-peak.md.
confidence: High on the population peak (42.38M in 2059, declining to 41.43M by 2070) and the continuous below-replacement run since 2013, both from DOSM. Medium on the precise TFR 1.6 (2024) and live births 414,918 (2024) pending direct confirmation against the DOSM Vital Statistics PDF (the long decline and the 2059 peak are independently corroborated).

source_notes: 3R HANDLING: DOSM's data includes divergent fertility by community and a projected ethnic-Chinese share falling under 15%. This is factual and openly reported, but per T4A 3R discipline (and the lesson of issue 1986, structural not racial framing) the CARDS stay national and do NOT single out any community. Ethnic risk is MEDIUM precisely because the cards avoid the ethnic breakdown; any ethnic-specific card would raise it to HIGH and require Stage 5 (Contrarian) escalation. Fertility is framed via structural drivers, not women's individual choices. The 2059 peak is DOSM's OFFICIAL projection, presented as a projection, not an observed fact.
